3a: Onboarding. The first thing you make is your pass. New here (3a-1 to 3a-9, about 45 seconds): name, a guide as your photo, this or that, home base, all filling in a passport page that’s issued and stamped before we ask for an account, a phone sign-in if you skip Apple and Google, then permissions with a live demo. Invited (3a-10 to 3a-13, about 15 seconds): a crew ticket with your name on it, or a typed code, a pass in three taps with what the inviter knows prefilled, and the crew manifest.
3b: Home. A first-run board of guides, then the everyday home: the trip coming up, the argument about the next one, and an inbox of things that need you, including what it looks like once nothing does. Once two places are left, Home shows the final. Somewhere else plans a place no guide lives in yet.
3c: Next trip: vote and setup. A place wins, then dates (and what happens when no week fits), budget, rooms and must-dos. The guide drafts the plan and you check it before anyone else sees it. Each person adds their must-do from a prompt, and any day of the draft can go back to Pon.
3d: Explore. Destination guides, swiping as a group, place pages with crowd forecasts, and a map your guide walks around.
3e: Plan. The trip day by day, a drag-to-plan day view, and a review step for every change the guide proposes.
3f: Proposal. The organiser builds it, each friend gets their own version, and replies are tracked with the guide suggesting nudges. A maybe gets a private word with the guide, and a dropout gets the plan re-split around them.
3g: Crew. A group chat the guide lives in, and live voting with cursors and comments. The crew pill on Home opens the chat, the crew name switches crews, and during a trip the chat’s MAP shows where everyone is.
3h: Bookings and getting around. One wallet for every booking, imports from email, and rides with a phrase card for the driver.
3i: Money. Balances, adding and scanning expenses (and a scan that fails), settling up and the budget, all in the same currency view.
3j: The guide. Text, voice and camera: three ways to ask, all able to propose changes to the group.
3k: During the trip. The hub, the day-of screen, the lock screen, no signal at the summit, a flight that slips, and help when something goes wrong. Then the forecast, and what happens when the sea, the roads or a scooter don’t cooperate.
3l: Critters and your pass. Hatch on landing, collect by being there (or miss one by leaving too soon), and chase crew quests. The pass is now the full Critterdex: 150 locals, each in four forms. Rare changes colour, epic adds a pose and a pink edge, and legendary goes gold and only shows on one day a year or for the hardest thing a place has.
3m: After. The recap summary and the shared album, then the recap as an eight-card story Tokek narrates: cover, route, crew awards, a printed receipt, the critter that got away, the passport stamp the crew signs, and a postcard. A year later it comes back as a memory.
3n: You. Profile with your passport stamps, settings (guide, sound, language and currency, account), editing your profile and avatar, app icon styles that match the store icons, and deleting your account with a 30-day way back.
3o: Community. Plans other crews shared after their trips, one of them opened and copied from, rating a trip in thirty seconds, and publishing your own with control over what leaves the crew.
3p: Help and feedback. A help hub, sending feedback with a screenshot already attached, a thank-you, an idea board that votes like the crew does, duplicate-catching when you suggest one, and the App Store rating prompt at the recap.
4e: Paywall, final: the visa page. Picked over the boarding pass and gold cover because the app is already a passport: critters are stamps, the boost success is an entry stamp, the icon is a passport. One page holds both offers, where the other two favour one. This pass adds a holographic visa with a light sweep, machine-readable lines, the stamps landing in order, and a welcome page.
4a: Paywall, three directions. 4e picks the visa page. The same offer as a visa page with stickers and a stamp, as two boarding passes, and as your pass getting a gold cover. Pick one and the rest of the flow follows it.
4b: Upgrading. A limit reached mid-question, the full comparison, boosting a trip with the cost split in Balances, the store sheet, and the stamp.
4c: The crew side. What a friend sees when someone boosts the trip, and the reminder before a crew’s free first trip runs out.
4d: Managing it. Your plan in Settings, cancelling (with a pause until the next trip), a declined card, and redeeming a gift code or restoring on a new phone.
4f: Entry points. The three limits a crew actually hits, each asked at the moment it matters with a quiet way out, and the full list of every way in.
5a: Live Activities and the Dynamic Island. Leave-by with Tokek walking the trail, the crew converging on a meet-up, flight day, a critter encounter that keeps counting in your pocket, the expanded island, the boost ask, and every compact state.
5b: Notifications. Written by the guide, grouped into an evening roundup, voted on without unlocking, an alarm that gets you up for Batur, and a ping budget.
5c: Widgets and StandBy. Before the trip, on the trip, on the lock screen, on the nightstand, and the gallery, with what is free and what comes with Pass+ or a boost.
